correctness.rationale: The construction was reconstructed from definitions. Direct sums preserve partial isometry and add ranks. The Jordan shifts have ranks 1 and 2 and numerical ranges D(0,1/2) and D(0,sqrt(2)/2). Reducing the focal parameter interval to a<3/4-sqrt(2)/2 puts both centered discs strictly inside D(a,3/4). The direct-sum numerical range is the convex hull of the summand ranges, so the focal disc remains unchanged. The parity calculation gives dimension 6+ceil(3(r-4)/2). The published rank-at-most-three theorem supplies the converse obstruction.

value.rationale: The result completes a natural rank classification suggested by the focal paper: the known positive regime ends exactly at rank 3, and the new construction shows that every rank from 4 upward actually occurs. This rules out rank four being an isolated pathology and supplies an explicit dimension bound for every rank. The statement is structural rather than a parameter tweak, even though its proof uses an elementary direct-sum mechanism.
